And she looked the part. She wore a black turtleneck every single day, just like Steve Jobs. She spoke in a deep, calm voice. She barely blinked. She worked almost every day of the year, and she expected the same from everyone around her. Silicon Valley fell in love.

The money poured in. Rupert Murdoch. The Walton family of Walmart. The DeVos family. In total, Theranos raised around nine hundred million dollars. Her board was full of legends. Two former secretaries of state, Henry Kissinger and George Shultz, and a future secretary of defense, General James Mattis. Then Walgreens signed a deal to put Theranos blood tests inside its pharmacies.

By 2014, Theranos was worth nine billion dollars, and Elizabeth owned about half of it. At thirty, she was the youngest self-made woman billionaire in the world. She was on magazine covers, on giant stages, and on live TV. Everyone wanted to know her secret.
